title: Black hole mass measurement using ALMA observations of [CI] and CO emissions in the Seyfert 1 galaxy NGC 7469
question: Measure the supermassive black hole mass in the Seyfert 1 galaxy NGC 7469 using ALMA observations of [CI](1-0) and 12CO(1-0) gas kinematics, test whether [CI](1-0) is a better dynamical tracer than CO in AGNs, and constrain the broad-line region virial factor and inclination.

data.sensitivity: RMS = 34 mJy beam^-1 km s^-1 for 12CO(1-0); RMS = 227 mJy beam^-1 km s^-1 for [CI](1-0)

what.value: Dust mass of ~2.5 x 10^7 M_sun within r <= 7''

evidence.quote: (cite: Papadopoulos00) also estimated the dust mass of $\approx2.5\times10^7$ M$_{\odot}$ in the same region of $r\leq7\ensuremath{''}$ ($\lesssim2.3$ kpc).

what.value: CO-to-H2 and [CI]-to-H2 conversion factors at the innermost ~100 pc region of NGC 7469: X_CO = 1.9 x 10^20 cm^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1 and X_[CI](1-0) = 2.1 x 10^20 cm^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1, plus galaxy centre coordinates and sigma_gas/V_rot ratios

evidence.quote: Using the dynamics of \[CI\](1-0) and $^{12}$CO(2-1), I20 found $\sigma_{\rm gas}/V_{\rm rot}\approx0.35$ ($r\lesssim0.5\ensuremath{''}$) and $\sigma_{\rm gas}/V_{\rm rot}\approx0.19$ ($r>0.5\ensuremath{''}$) (see panels a and b of their Fig. 11)

Based on dynamical modellings, I20 found the CO-to- and \[CI\]-to-H$_2$ conversion factor of $X_{\rm CO}=1.9\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$ (K km s$^{-1}$)$^{-1}$ and $X_{\rm [CI](1-0)}=2.1\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$ (K km s$^{-1}$)$^{-1}$, respectively, at the innermost $\approx100$ pc region of NGC 7469.

what.value: Reverberation mapping M_BH = (1.0 +- 0.1) x 10^7 M_sun and BLR R_BLR and Delta V errors

evidence.quote: Whereas, the RM method used the indirect signature from the broad line region (BLR) variability using H$\beta$ and He ii$~\lambda$4686 emissions (cite: Peterson04; Peterson14; Wang14), giving a $M_{\rm BH}=(1.0\pm0.1)\times10^7$ M$_{\odot}$.

Given our dynamical $M_{\rm BH}$ constraint of $1.78\times10^7$M$_{\odot}$ and its $1\sigma$ uncertainty (Table \[fittable\]) and account for the consistency with $1\sigma$ errors of $R_{\rm BLR}$ and $\Delta V$ (cite: Peterson14), we find $f=7.2^{+4.2}_{-3.4}$ for the BLR in NGC 7469

what.value: Bulge/spheroid stellar velocity dispersion sigma_* = 152 +- 16 km s^-1

evidence.quote: Also, (cite: Onken04) used slit-spectroscopy to estimate its bulge/spheroid velocity dispersion of $\sigma_\star=152\pm16$ km s$^{-1}$ using the stellar absorption lines of Ca ii triplet (CaT) in the NIR regime excited by the AGN.

what.value: Colour-M/L scaling relations for converting F547M-F814W colour maps into M/L and mass-surface-density maps

evidence.loc: The stellar-mass models account for spatial variations of populations and extinction
evidence.quote: In principle, we could apply the colour–$M/L$ scaling relations for the young nucleus ($<$1 Gyr) compiled by B01 and N19 to convert this colour map into their corresponding $M/L$ maps (panels a and b of Fig. 15)

recipe.goal: Reduce HST images and construct PSF models
recipe.method: Download raw flt frames of HST ACS F814W and WFC3 F547M, re-reduce ACS F814W with Astrodrizzle to 0.04'' pixel scale, align to the ALMA galaxy centre from Izumi et al. (2020), and generate combined PSF models (FWHM = 0.08'') by inserting Tiny Tim PSFs into flc frames and drizzling.
assumptions: Galactic extinction A_V = 0.184 (A_F547M = 0.075 mag, A_F814W = 0.105 mag) and Cardelli et al. (1989) extinction law

recipe.goal: Create ALMA 3D cubes, moment maps, PVDs, and radial PA profiles
recipe.method: Create 3D (R.A., decl., velocity) cubes for 12CO(1-0) and [CI](1-0) using CASA; generate moment 0, 1, and 2 maps using the moments masking technique (spatial smoothing by factor alpha and clipping at beta*sigma on the smoothed cube to mask the full-resolution cube); extract major- and minor-axis PVDs (3-pixel / 0.81'' width); extract radial position angle profiles from velocity fields using Kinemetry.
key_parameters: Smoothing factor alpha = 3, clipping threshold beta = 0.5 sigma; PVD cut width = 3 pixels (0.81'') along major axis PA = 308 deg and minor axis PA = 218 deg

recipe.goal: Construct the default galaxy stellar and ISM mass models
recipe.method: Fit the HST WFC3 F547M PSF with a circular Multi-Gaussian Expansion (MGE), then fit the F547M galaxy image with an axisymmetric MGE using mge_fit_sectors while masking the central AGN (r < 0.06''), starburst ring, and bright stars. Estimate H2 mass from 12CO(1-0) aperture fluxes and combine with literature dust mass via the KinMS gasgrav mechanism.
key_parameters: 6 Gaussian components for F547M PSF (Table 2); 7 Gaussian components for F547M stellar light (Table 3); central AGN mask r < 0.06''; M_H2(r <= 3'') = 2.7 x 10^9 M_sun, M_H2(r <= 7'') = 4 x 10^9 M_sun; M_dust(r <= 7'') = 2.5 x 10^7 M_sun
assumptions: Starburst CO-to-H2 conversion factor X_CO = 1.0 +- 0.3 x 10^20 cm^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1; gas-to-dust ratio ~ 160; ISM distributed according to 12CO(1-0) and [CI](1-0) surface brightness; constant stellar M/L_F547M

recipe.goal: Fit 3D gas kinematics with KinMS and MCMC to measure M_BH
recipe.method: Simulate 3D gas cubes in KinMS using circular velocities from mge_circular_velocity (JAM package), radial PA profiles from Kinemetry, and a Gaussian radial gas surface brightness profile; fit 9 free parameters (log M_BH, M/L_F547M, sigma_gas, G_sigma, F, i, x_c, y_c, v_off) to the 12CO(1-0) and [CI](1-0) cubes via KINMSpy_MCMC and emcee.
key_parameters: Fit region = 60 x 60 pixels (6'' x 6'') and 60 velocity channels covering (-300, 300) km s^-1 (N = 60 x 60 x 60 constraints, P = 9 parameters); 3 x 10^5 MCMC iterations with 20% burn-in
assumptions: Gas moves on circular orbits in a dynamically thin, cold disc (asymmetric drift ignored); axisymmetric Gaussian gas surface brightness profile; D_A = 68.4 Mpc

recipe.goal: Test systematic uncertainties in stellar and ISM mass models on M_BH
recipe.method: Re-run KinMS on [CI](1-0) kinematics allowing only M_BH and M/L_F547M (or mass-scaling factor Gamma) to vary while fixing other parameters to best-fit values, testing: (1) Bell & de Jong (2001) and Nguyen et al. (2019) colour-based MGE mass maps from HST F547M-F814W, (2) Izumi et al. (2020) X_CO and X_[CI] conversion factors, (3) axisymmetric MGE ISM distribution with gasGrav turned off, and (4) unmasked central AGN light in F547M MGE.
key_parameters: Search range for Gamma = (0.1, 2.0); X_CO = 1.9 x 10^20 cm^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1; X_[CI](1-0) = 2.1 x 10^20 cm^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1; sky background annulus (20-22)''
assumptions: Bell & de Jong (2001) and Nguyen et al. (2019) colour-M/L relations; central saturated pixels in F814W interpolated from outer pixels

recipe.goal: Constrain the BLR virial factor f and inclination angle i
recipe.method: Combine the [CI](1-0) dynamical M_BH with reverberation-mapping R_BLR and Delta V measurements using the virial equation M_BH = f * R_BLR * (Delta V)^2 / G to solve for f, then derive the BLR inclination angle i using the planar thick-disc analytical relation in the thin-disc limit (h/R_BLR ~ 0).
assumptions: Virial equilibrium in the BLR; geometrically thin planar BLR disc with (h/R_BLR) ~ 0

answer_key.quantity: Reverberation mapping BLR dimensionless scaling factor f

evidence.quote: Given this new $M_{\rm BH}$, we are able to constrain the specific RM dimensionless scaling factor of $f=7.2^{+4.2}_{-3.4}$ for the AGN BLR in NGC 7469.

Given our dynamical $M_{\rm BH}$ constraint of $1.78\times10^7$M$_{\odot}$ and its $1\sigma$ uncertainty (Table \[fittable\]) and account for the consistency with $1\sigma$ errors of $R_{\rm BLR}$ and $\Delta V$ (cite: Peterson14), we find $f=7.2^{+4.2}_{-3.4}$ for the BLR in NGC 7469

The gas within the unresolved BLR thus has a Keplerian virial velocity component and the inclination of $i\approx11.0^\circ$$_{-2.5}^{+2.2}$, confirming its face-on orientation in a Seyfert 1 AGN by assuming a geometrically thin BLR model.

We thus consider the thin disc BLR model for the NGC 7469 AGN in which $(h/R_{\rm BLR})\approx0$, giving the BLR’s LOS inclination of $i\approx11.0^\circ$$_{-2.5}^{+2.2}$, which tightly constrains the face-on orientation of the BLR.

score_reason: The paper provides complete MGE tables (PSF and galaxy light), explicit MCMC priors, grid dimensions (60x60x60), error rescaling formula, and links to public modelling codes (KINMSpy_MCMC, MgeFit, Kinemetry), as well as public ALMA/HST project IDs. However, visibility reduction/imaging is deferred to Izumi et al. (2020) and exact radial PA arrays and HST pixel masks are not provided in machine-readable form.
rediscovery_reason: Both the ALMA data (2017.1.00078.S) and HST images (GO-11661, GO-10592) are public in their respective archives, the MGE tables and KinMS parameter search ranges are explicitly tabulated, and the main results (M_BH, M/L_F547M, f, BLR inclination) are clear quantitative targets.
